newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela July inflation rate 2.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela July inflation rate 2.8 pct.

text.p: Consumer prices in Venezuela rose 2.8 percent in July, down from 5.0 percent in July 1996 but up from 1.8 percent in June 1997, the Central Bank said.
Accumulated inflation for the first seven months of 1997 was 16.8 percent compared to 70.4 percent in the same period last year, Central Bank figures showed.
Accumulated inflation for the last 12 months was 40.5 percent compared to 112.6 percent in the year to July 1996.
July's monthly price rise was the second highest monthly rate so far this year. Prices rose 3.1 percent in May.
The acceleration of price rises in July was roughly in line with market expectations following recent increases in public services and wage rises in the private sector.
The Central Bank attributed July's price rises to higher electricity and gas rates, supply shortages of some foodstuffs and increases in school fees.
According to the Bank, which measures the indicator based on a survey of price rises in a broad range of goods and services in the capital, prices of "Various expenditures" rose 4.2 percent in July.
The category "Food, drinks tobacco" rose 2.8 percent, "Household expenditures," 1.8 percent and "Shoes and clothing," 1.5 percent.
The government has set a target of bringing annual inflation down from 103.2 percent in 1996 to between 30 and 35 percent this year.
But local and international analysts have warned that wage rises and a lack of control over fiscal accounts could jeopardize that goal.
